lastCommit.message:
[ota-hal] OTA-1649: what a ring is for

Owner: "do the ring and amulet recipes, and give the diadem a route. again
better effects with rarity and ingredient quality. they should give
combinations of stat buffs, moderate resists and let's get some special
AOE effects... each ring doesn't need to have all three things. the
combinations of 1, 2 or three things should scale with rarity."

⚠ WHAT THE MEASUREMENT FOUND FIRST, before a line was written. Fifteen of
the thirty-two shipped accessories carry a `resistances` list. The item
card prints it — "Resists: aetheric" — and combat has NEVER SEEN ONE.
aggregateArmor's resist walk covered ARMOR_SLOTS only, so a Legendary
aetheric amulet arrived at the damage math as `[]` with a mitigation
fraction of 0. Probed before any change; that probe is now the first test
in ota1649 so the field cannot go quiet again.

So "moderate resists" was not a new feature. It was a dead field, and
wiring it is the spine of this OTA.

  • The jewellery joins the EXISTING armour stack — same multiplicative
    diminishing returns, same MAX_ARMOR_RESIST ceiling — through a new
    optional per-entry `weight` on ArmorSlotResist. Armour never sets it
    (a chest is a chest whatever it is made of); jewellery always does,
    because a ring's worth against a type is its RARITY, not which finger
    it sits on. Every pre-existing caller is bit-identical.
  • An amulet outweighs a ring at equal rarity — one neck, four fingers —
    and neither out-armours a breastplate. His "50% of incoming fire" is
    measured, not asserted: a Legendary amulet + a Legendary ring + a Rare
    ring = 0.497. Three slots given to one element buys half. One
    Legendary ring alone buys a fifth.

THREE NEW EFFECT FAMILIES, wired and pinned:

  • A COATING BOOST. His fire ring, exactly: a Rare burn ring is +25% on
    burn coatings and nothing else. Applied to the rolled coating bonus
    only (a bare blade gets nothing) and AFTER the weakness multiplier, so
    a resistant hide cannot halve the ring's share as well.
  • A STEALTH MULTIPLIER. Legendary = his +60%. It multiplies the whole
    strike, and it does NOT check the weapon: the dice-doubling backstab
    is a rogue's privilege, this is not, or it would be a second rogue tax
    on an item a heavy build might want. ⚠ The flag rides the DAMAGE STEP:
    `stealthed` is stripped by consumeOnResolve the instant the attack
    step resolves and pendingRolls is nulled before concludeRolls runs, so
    a damage-time read of the player would miss the exact swing the ring
    was bought for. combatRules stamps `fromStealth` at build time.
  • A ONCE-PER-ENCOUNTER DISCHARGE. His frost ring: 50 cold across two
    rings of range. It fires on the first swing of the fight — there is no
    free action in this combat loop to hang a trigger on, and committing
    to the fight is the honest trigger. Not the weapon splash: that is
    keyed to the TARGET's band, this to the WEARER's. All discharges are
    planned off one lineup and applied in one write, so the first ring's
    kill cannot hide a body from the second. A burst that catches nobody
    is still spent — refunding it would make a ring strictly better than a
    splash, which pays the same price.

⚠⚠ THE ROW PICKS THE FLAVOUR, THE LADDER PICKS THE NUMBER. Not one catalog
row carries a magnitude. A ring says "I boost burn coatings"; how much is
COATED_BOOST_PCT[rarity]. That is what makes "better effects with rarity"
a property of the system rather than a promise about forty-four
hand-typed numbers — a row cannot sit off the ladder, and a rebalance is
one table edit.

⚠ THE LADDER'S GATE IS THE SPECIAL, NOT A FAMILY COUNT, and the first
draft got that wrong. An exact count per rarity failed against the shipped
catalog on contact: five accessories — two of them COMMON — already
carried two families, and holding the line would have meant deleting a
resist off items sitting in players' packs right now. So the rule moved to
where the owner's sentence actually points. Common and Uncommon never
carry a special; Rare may; Legendary must, and carries all three. Every
band is still strictly better than the one below on MAGNITUDE too, on all
five tables, so a two-family Uncommon never out-values a two-family Rare.
The rule needed no removals at all: the seven rows it found off-ladder
were each missing something, and each gained it.

THE ROUTES. 16 new accessories (48 total) and a recipe for every ring and
amulet in the game — 205 recipes. The Aetheric Diadem was the only
genuinely unobtainable item in the catalog (no recipe, no loot table, no
vendor, no quest) and now has one. Ingredient quality is mechanical: every
accessory recipe must carry at least one ingredient of the result's own
rarity or higher, so a Legendary cannot be reached from scrap. One shipped
recipe failed that and was repaired rather than grandfathered —
Reclaimer's Aegis Pendant is Rare and asked for Scrap Metal / Aetheric
Shard / Spider Silk.

⚠⚠⚠ THE MISTAKE I MADE AND HAD TO UNDO, kept as a rule. The first draft of
those 38 recipes reached for whatever material fitted the flavour and
claimed 22 fresh names — Aetheric Blood, Spirit Residue, Warden Stone,
Aetheric Cog and eighteen more. `isRecipeIngredientName` bars any recipe
ingredient from the Crucible, so every one of them silently LEFT the
fusion fodder pool, and seven shipped fusion suites went red. They were
right; the Crucible had genuinely lost its fodder. The fix was not to
repoint them. Every recipe was re-authored out of the 96 names recipes
already used, so the fodder pool after this OTA is bit-identical to the
one before it — measured, `newly claimed: []`. ota1649 pins it, so the
next accessory recipe reaching for a fresh material has to answer for the
Crucible first. A second pin catches the other thing that pass produced: a
blind substitution left seven recipes naming one ingredient twice.

The line ratchet did its job too. This walked gameStore through the 37,000
cap (ota1400), which is what the cap is for. The discharge's targeting and
application moved out to `planBursts` / `applyBursts` in accessoryEffects,
where they are pure and testable rather than reachable only through a live
combat turn. gameStore lands at 36,996.

The item card now names numbers instead of a bare "Resists: aetheric",
reading the same tables combat reads so the two cannot drift, and a
discharge card admits on its face that it is once per fight.

Gates: all 18 green by exit code. Full suite green.
